'''Agni Vlavianos Arvanitis''' (9 March 1936 – 7 April 2018)<ref>{{cite web |title=Farewell Agni Vlavianos Arvanitis 1936 – 2018 – BIOPOLITICS INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATION (B.I.O.) |url=https://biopolitics.gr/biowp/farewell-agni-vlavianos-arvanitis/ |website=BIOPOLITICS INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATION (B.I.O.) |accessdate=28 June 2018 |date=12 April 2018}}</ref> was a professor and researcher in [[biology]]. Her main contribution lies in the field of [[biopolitics]], and the theory of [[bios (philosophy)|bios]]. She graduated from [[Barnard College]] in 1957 (B.A.), [[New York University]] (M.S.) and the [[University of Athens]] (Ph.D.). She worked as a researcher at the [[Museum of Natural History in New York]], the [[University of California at Berkeley]], and the [[University of Paris]]. She has also taught Biology, Biochemistry and Human Genetics at the [[Friends Seminary]] in New York, the [[American Community Schools Academy]] in Athens, and the [[University of Maryland]].<ref name="pellam-500">John L. Pellam Bibliotheque: Worldwide International Publishers (2011) "The Preeminent 500: 500 Exceptional Individuals of Achievement in Commerce Science & Technology, Medicine and the Arts & Letters" pg.53, {{ISBN|1-882292-27-8}}</ref><ref name="pellam-encyclopedia">John L. Pellam Bibliotheque: Worldwide International Publishers "Encyclopedia Intelligentsia A Compendium of Great Thinkers and Bright Minds of the 21st Century", pg.43, {{ISBN|978-1-882292-39-4}}</ref><ref name="marshall">Global Marshall Plan Foundation "Towards a World in Balance: A Virtual Congress for a Better Balanced World", pg.169, {{ISBN|3-9809723-7-2}}</ref>

== The biopolitics theory ==
Her theory of biopolitics sees biopolitics as a conceptual and operative framework for societal development, promoting bios (Greek = life) as the central theme in every human endeavor, be it policy, education, art, government, science or technology. This concept uses bios as a term referring to all forms of life on our planet, including their genetic and geographic variation.<ref name="unesco">UNESCO Eolss Publishers Co. Ltd, (2001) OUR FRAGILE WORLD Challenges and Opportunities for Sustainable Development Vol.1, Pg.1027. {{ISBN|0-9534944-7-0}}</ref>

== Achievements ==
In 1985, Agni Vlavianos Arvanitis founded the Biopolitics International Organisation (B.I.O.) with the goal of promoting respect for the gift of bios (life) and international cooperation for the protection of the environment. B.I.O created an international network of associates in over 160 countries around the world, with scholars and decision-makers supporting its goals and projects.<ref name="pellam-500" /><ref name="pellam-encyclopedia" /><ref name="marshall" />

== Recognition ==
Agni Vlavianos Arvanitis was the recipient of a number of international distinctions including election as Honorary President for Life of the [[United Nations Association]] in Sri Lanka; election as an International Patron of the [[Global Cooperation for a Better World]]; the commemorative Gold Medal of Honor for outstanding achievements and dedication to personal and professional goals, as well as election as 1994 Woman of the year by [[Anita Borg Institute|ABI]].<ref name="pellam-encyclopedia" /> Notably she has been appointed [[Doctor Honoris Causa]] of [[Mendeleyev University]] in Moscow, and Honorary professor of [[St. Petersburg State Technological University of Plant Polymers]].<ref name="unesco" />
